review.title: Crawling down the G-file, then into the corner
review.summary: The 12k won by resignation, with Black ahead by 5.3 after the last move. The game was level until move 9. After that, Opus 5.5 gave away points in two swings. One was the G-file crawl, where G4 lost 4.0 and G2 lost 5.8. The other was B3 and B2 on the left, which lost 9.4 and 9.1. The 12k gave back large chunks with C2, B1 and D6 (6.2, 9.4 and 7.4), but never lost the lead.

moments.text: Opus 5.5 had turned the position around: Black's lead was -2.7 before G2, meaning White was ahead. G2 extended White's wall along the G-file to the second line, lost 5.8 points and put Black ahead by 3.1. The engine preferred B5.

Opus 5.5 played B3 against the Black stones on C3 and C5, lost 9.4 points, and Black's lead went from 3.9 to 13.3. The engine's choice was F6, in the middle of the board, rather than another move on the left edge.

Opus 5.5 followed with B2 and lost 9.1 more, taking Black's lead from 7.1 to 16.2. The White stones on B2, B3 and B4 now form a thin line on the left edge. Black's C-file stones sit beside them, and the engine would have played D3.
The 12k played B1, which lost 9.4 and cut Black's lead from 16.2 to 6.8. The engine's choice was E7. It was the biggest single swing back toward White in the game, and it kept Opus 5.5 in it.

After Opus 5.5's D5 (4.4 lost), the 12k's D6 lost 7.4 points and the lead dropped from 11.4 to 4.0. It was the 12k's third blunder and brought the game closest to level, though Black still led. Opus 5.5 answered C6, which lost 1.4 more, and Black led by 5.3 when White resigned.

audit.reason: libs.py and count.py only parse a pasted board and report groups, liberties and area counts of the current position, and the other commands just cat/tail notes and append to games.md and CLAUDE.md; nothing chooses, ranks or looks ahead at moves.
